subject: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan
messages:
From: Alice Keller <alice.keller@cloudline.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudline.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan

Hannah —

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Procurement at Cloudline asked me to start a short thread to get alignment on availability and monthly remedy mechanics before we engage legal. Two main asks from our side: 1) a baseline uptime commitment at 99.95% for API endpoints used in production, and 2) a clear monthly credit calculation with a predictable cap (we have internal auditors who need a firm monthly maximum).

We also need explicit carveouts for scheduled maintenance (we can accept planned maintenance known 72+ hours in advance) and a defined incident reporting SLA (initial triage within 1 hour; full RCA timeline).

Could you share Redwood's standard template and any proposal on the credit ladder you typically offer (monthly credits expressed as percentage of invoice or $ cap)?

Attachments: none (procurement will attach their standard SOW template if helpful).

Best,
Alice Keller
Sr. Vendor Sourcing Manager
Cloudline Financial

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Keller <alice.keller@cloudline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudline.com
Date: 2026-12-01T12:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks — very reasonable to get alignment before Legal digs in. High-level proposal from Redwood:

- Hosted API (standard tier): 99.9% monthly uptime. Remedy: graduated credit ladder starting at 5% of monthly invoice for 99.0–99.89%, scaling to 25% for sub-95%. Monthly credit capped at 25% of invoice.
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity: can be bumped to 99.95% uptime with a modified credit ladder (smaller per-band credits, cap at 20%).

Carveouts: planned maintenance (notified >=72 hours) and force majeure events are excluded. We will include an incident reporting clause: initial triage within 1 hour, incident update cadence every 2 hours until mitigation, and substantive RCA within 7 business days for Sev1.

I'm attaching an internal draft SLA (SLA-draft-v1.pdf) and a simple credit-matrix spreadsheet (credit-matrix.xlsx) that shows per-band calculations. If Cloudline requires 99.95 on Hosted, we can discuss a higher monthly fee or a commitment to Dedicated capacity.

Next steps: if this matches your expectations, I'll loop in Ben (sales) and Marissa (legal ops) to refine the wording and surface any commercial tradeoffs (credits vs. price).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Attachments: SLA-draft-v1.pdf, credit-matrix.xlsx

From: Alice Keller <alice.keller@cloudline.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudline.com
Date: 2026-12-02T08:56:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick reply and the attachments — we reviewed the draft. A couple of clarifying points from Procurement and Risk:

1) Cloudline is a regulated financial services firm; 99.95% is our security and audit team's expectation for any externally-hosted inference endpoints used in production. It's non-negotiable for endpoints handling regulated payment flows.

2) On remedies: Procurement prefers a dollar-denominated monthly cap instead of a percentage so our budget and escrow accounting lines are clear. Would Redwood be open to a cap expressed as (monthly commit * X) or a fixed $ ceiling?

3) We need language that allows a temporary canary period (first 90 days) where metrics and thresholds can be reviewed and adjusted, but during that period Cloudline still needs a minimum availability guarantee (we'd accept a staged ramp if it helps).

If you can propose concrete wording for a $ cap and confirm the 90-day review mechanics, we can put this into our SOW and move to legal redlines.

Regards,
Alice

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Keller <alice.keller@cloudline.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudline.com
Date: 2026-12-02T11:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan

Alice / Hannah —

Brief proposed compromise and concrete numbers to unblock Legal:

- Availability: For Dedicated-only deployments (reserved capacity), Redwood will commit to 99.95% monthly uptime. For Hosted multi-tenant API we will remain at 99.9% unless Cloudline takes an enhanced SLA add-on (pricing delta applies).

- Dollar-denominated monthly cap: propose cap = min($50,000, 50% of monthly committed spend) for the first 12 months. This provides a hard ceiling procurement can budget to and scales with commitment. We can convert to a simple formula in the SOW: "Monthly Remedy Cap = min($50,000, 0.5 * Monthly Commitment)."

- Canary/review: First 90 days post-go-live = "Stability Ramp". During this period, we agree to weekly checkpoint calls, instrumentation access for a designated Cloudline engineer, and a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first-month invoice if Cloudline accepts Hosted at 99.9% rather than Dedicated at 99.95%.

- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance (>=72 hours notice) not counted; emergency maintenance will be logged and will not exceed 4 hours/month without counting against uptime if pre-approved via the ops channel.

I'll add these into SLA-draft-v2 and circulate. Open to moving the $ cap number if it's too low/high — wanted to put a concrete anchor on the table.

Onwards — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: Alice Keller <alice.keller@cloudline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudline.com
Date: 2026-12-02T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan

Ben / Hannah —

That structure is helpful and gets us much closer. A couple of small asks before we route to Legal: 1) Can we see the exact clause text for the "Monthly Remedy Cap" (we prefer it inline in the SLA rather than as a reference to a formula)? 2) Add explicit language that scheduled maintenance does not exceed 6 hours/month aggregated and that any emergency maintenance exceeding that will require 48-hour post-event remediation plan.

Also confirm the RCA timeline for Sev1 remains 7 business days and whether Sev2 RCAs will be delivered within 15 business days. Procurement will likely accept the onboarding credit but will want it tied to acceptance criteria (e.g., post-integration smoke tests pass).

If you can send a v2 with these clauses verbatim, procurement will produce a single SOW with the DocuSign flow and we'll be ready to exchange redlines.

Thanks,
Alice

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Keller <alice.keller@cloudline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudline.com
Date: 2026-12-03T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stability anchor and monthly remedy workplan

Alice —

Appreciate the clear feedback. I've drafted the verbatim clauses and attached SLA-draft-v2.pdf for your review. Highlights included in v2:

- Monthly Remedy Cap (verbatim): "Monthly Remedy Cap shall not exceed the lesser of Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (US$50,000) or fifty percent (50%) of Customer's Monthly Commitment as set forth in the applicable Order Form."

- Maintenance window language (verbatim): "Planned maintenance shall not exceed six (6) hours per calendar month aggregated. Emergency maintenance may be performed as necessary; if emergency maintenance cumulatively exceeds six (6) hours in any calendar month, Provider shall submit a remediation plan within forty-eight (48) hours of the end of the month in which such excess occurred."

- RCA timelines: Sev1 = 7 business days; Sev2 = 15 business days (both from incident closure date).

- Canary / Stability Ramp: added acceptance criteria for onboarding credit: "Onboarding credit (10% of first-month invoice) is contingent upon successful completion of integration smoke tests as documented in Annex A and Customer's written acceptance within 30 days of go-live."

If Cloudline is comfortable with the language in v2, please confirm and we'll escalate to Legal to accept redlines. If you want any numbers adjusted (cap amount or percent), let us know and Ben will run the commercial impact.

Attachments: SLA-draft-v2.pdf

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
